examples.problem: Find the total charge $Q$ of a metal plate that occupies the region $D = \{ (x,y) : 0 \le x \le 1, \, 0 \le y \le 2\}$ with charge density $\rho (x,y) = 4 - 3y^2 + 2x.$
examples.worked_solution:
The total charge $Q$ of a plate that occupies the region $D = \{ (x,y) : 0 \leq x \leq 1, \, 0 \leq y \leq 2\}$ with charge density $\rho (x,y) = 4 - 3y^2 + 2x$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Q & ={∬}_{D}(4-3{y}^{2}+2x)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:

$$
\iint\limits_{D} (4 - 3y^2 + 2x) \:\textrm{d}A
= \int_{0}^2 \left[ \int_{0}^1 (4 - 3y^2 + 2x) \:\textrm{d}x \right] \textrm{d}y
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1}(4-3{y}^{2}+2x)\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[4x-3{y}^{2}x+{x}^{2}]_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[(4(1)-3{y}^{2}(1)+(1)^{2})-(4(0)-3{y}^{2}(0)-(0)^{2})]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(5-3{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}(5-3{y}^{2})\,\text{d}y & =[5y-{y}^{3}]_{0}^{2} \\  & =(5(2)-(2)^{3})-(5(0)-(0)^{3}) \\  & =(10-8)-0 \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the charge of the plate is $Q=2.$
